gap: No result ChatGPT got states, in the maker's own words, that a headset works on Xbox only if its own radio, or its USB dongle, uses Microsoft's Xbox Wireless link. So the PlayStation version of a headset that ChatGPT recommended, the Turtle Beach Stealth 600 Gen 3, 'will NOT work on any Xbox console', and only the X-suffixed SteelSeries Nova 5X (not the Nova 5 or 5P) has a dongle that carries Xbox audio.
standout_why: I read RTINGS 'The 6 Best Headsets For Xbox Series X/S' (cited) and Tom's Guide 'Best gaming headsets in 2026' (cited) through WebFetch. Only the navigation and menus came back, with no article text about Xbox Wireless, dongles or PlayStation versions, so I can't say they lack this. ChatGPT's own answer says only that Bluetooth doesn't work and that you should 'choose an Xbox-compatible model'. Its Stealth 600 card does not say which platform version it is. Adellion (rank 10, not cited) already explains the mechanism in general terms: 'Xbox consoles send wireless audio over Microsoft's own Xbox Wireless protocol', 'Most PlayStation-branded dongles skip that license', and the Stealth 600 PS version 'looks nearly identical'. So part of this is already out there. What's new is the makers' own statements for the exact products ChatGPT picked.
decides: This confirms the picks but adds a rule the shopper has to follow when buying. The Stealth 600 Gen 3 and the Arctis Nova 5 only work if they're the Xbox SKU ('for Xbox' / '5X'). That SKU also works on PlayStation, but the reverse isn't true, so a shopper with both consoles should buy the Xbox version. Any headset whose dongle isn't labelled for Xbox, including Dealectric's EKSA 2.4 GHz models (E900 BT, E1000 WT, Mako BT), only reaches Xbox through its 3.5 mm cable plugged into the controller. That makes the wired EKSA Fenrir S, and the 3.5 mm route generally, the honest pick from our catalogue.

findings.label: Why Bluetooth headsets don't work on Xbox
findings.value: Xbox consoles 'do not support Bluetooth audio for game sound or chat'; 'The console uses its own XBOX Wireless protocol, which delivers lower latency than Bluetooth.'
findings.source_title: Can You Connect Bluetooth Headphones to XBOX? The Truth (Turtle Beach, Maya Deiss, 2026-05-29)
findings.note: This is a headset maker's own explanation. Microsoft's support page that xbox.com/headset-compatibility redirects to (support.xbox.com/.../connect-compatible-headset) loads its text with JavaScript, and WebFetch got no body text.

findings.label: Wired route through the controller
findings.value: Wired headphones plug into the controller's 3.5 mm jack and pull 'game audio and chat through the controller'; the sound 'runs through the controller's built-in DAC'.
findings.source_title: Can You Connect Bluetooth Headphones to XBOX? The Truth (Turtle Beach)
findings.note: This is how wired picks such as the EKSA Fenrir S and the Xbox Stereo Headset connect.

findings.label: PlayStation version on Xbox
findings.value: 'The Stealth 600 Gen 3 for PlayStation will NOT work on any Xbox console.' The Xbox version works on both Xbox and PlayStation.
findings.source_title: Best Buy Q&A: Turtle Beach Stealth 600 Gen 3 for PS5/PS4/PC (answer by Turtle Beach Support)
findings.note: Answered by the verified brand account Turtle Beach Support. The page only says 'Answered 1 year ago'.

findings.label: Xbox connection and price
findings.value: USB-A wireless transmitter 'for XBOX Series X|S and One'; 2.4 GHz plus Bluetooth 5.2 with QuickSwitch; $109.99
findings.note: The page notes that 'Select advanced audio features available in 2.4GHz wireless mode may not be supported in Bluetooth® mode.' Battery is claimed at 80 h.

findings.label: Which Nova 5 variant carries Xbox audio
findings.value: The dongle is 'your key to audio on PC, PlayStation, Xbox (with the Nova 5X)'. The base Nova 5 is not listed for Xbox.
findings.source_title: Introducing Arctis Nova 5 Wireless Gaming Headset (SteelSeries blog, 2024-04-25)
findings.note: steelseries.com/gaming-headsets/arctis-nova-5x returned a page listing only PS5/PS4, PC and Switch with no Xbox mention, so it appears to show the base Nova 5. Its listed specs are 60 h battery and 265 g / 9.5 oz.

findings.label: Connection
findings.value: 'Direct pairing to console' with no dongle; Bluetooth 5.3 (A2DP, HFP, HSP, SBC) for PC and mobile; 'Windows 10/11 use requires Bluetooth 4.2+ or compatible USB-C cable'; up to 20 h battery
findings.note: The page shows no price. It says Bluetooth is for PC and mobile music and chat, not for the console.

findings.label: Xbox route
findings.value: For the Xbox One S/X controller, 'you can directly connect your headset to the controller via the 3.5 mm audio cable'. 'Old version of Xbox One needs a Microsoft adapter (not included)'. 'Not compatible with Xbox 360.'
findings.source_title: EKSA E1000 WT Wireless Gaming Headset Manual (ManualsLib)
findings.note: The manual's only Xbox instruction is the 3.5 mm cable to the controller. It gives no instruction for using the USB dongle on Xbox, and its platform list mixes cable and dongle together.

unsourced: Microsoft's own wording on support.xbox.com (headset compatibility / 'Designed for Xbox' licensing): the page loads its text with JavaScript and WebFetch got no body text.
Whether the EKSA E900 BT and Mako BT 2.4 GHz dongles carry audio on Xbox: eksa.net returned HTTP 429 to both WebFetch and storecheck.py, and I found no EKSA statement for those two models.
The Xbox-related text in the cited RTINGS and Tom's Guide articles: WebFetch got only navigation and menus, so I couldn't check what they say.
SteelSeries' US product page specifically for the Nova 5X, with its Xbox/USB switch wording, weight and price: the 5X URL returned a page with no Xbox mention.
